Definition: of uncertain affinity; in the oblique cases there is used instead of it a (probably cognate) name Δίς, which is otherwise obsolete; Zeus or Dis (among the Latins, Jupiter or Jove), the supreme deity of the Greeks:--Jupiter.
BiblicalUsage: Zeus — Jupiter to the Romans — is the supreme god of the Greeks, and he appears once in the New Testament, at Lystra. The crowd calls Barnabas Jupiter and Paul Mercury, and the priest of Jupiter brings oxen to sacrifice to them. The apostles tear their clothes: they are men, not gods.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Lystra shows the shape of idolatry: men will worship anything, even the messengers, rather than the God who sent them.
